ShortDescription.Value: Copy & paste props — select, move, rotate, blueprint and stamp groups of props

Publish.LongDescription:
## Copaste A copy & paste tool for props — select groups of props, copy them, and stamp them anywhere with preserved layout, rotation and height.
## Features - **Click & marquee selection** — click props or drag a camera-aligned box; live highlight while dragging. Works on props, decals AND trees - **Copy & paste with preview** — the copied group follows your mouse as a ghost; click to place, repeat to stamp - **Original colors kept on paste** — pasted props keep the source's color variation AND any custom color from the Customization tab; a blue bench stays blue (Original/Random toggle in the panel) - **Align tools** — Line makes a tidy row (straight line, equal gaps, uniform rotation); To prop anchors the row to a reference prop you click; Circle arranges props evenly on a circle. Resize the layout live with [ and ] or the panel stepper - **Move** — drag a selected prop to move the whole selection; Alt+drag moves just one prop - **Group rotation** — hold right mouse button and drag (Alt snaps to 45°), or use the panel buttons; Alt+mouse wheel spins each prop around its own axis - **Ctrl+click picking** — selects props partially buried in other objects or buildings; repeat on the same spot to cycle through stacked props - **Height controls** — raise/lower (PgUp/PgDn), snap to ground (End), match another prop's height (Home) - **Delete** — press Delete to remove the whole selection at once. Combined with marquee + type filter it's great for bulk cleanup: box-select an area, press T on a tree to keep only that tree type, hit Delete — a whole overgrown forest gone in three clicks (and Ctrl+Z brings it back, ages preserved) - **Type filter** — press T to toggle a filter taken from the hovered/selected prop: marquee then only picks that exact type (works for trees too). While the filter is active, clicking any prop switches the filter to that prop's type - **Undo** — Ctrl+Z reverts move, rotate, height, delete and paste (32 steps); deleted trees come back with their original growth stage - **Blueprints** — save prop groups to disk (colors included) and reuse them in any city or save - **Anarchy-style pasting** — ignores overlap errors while pasting (toggleable). Anarchy is NOT required: if it happens to be installed, Copaste additionally protects pasted props from being hidden by the game - **Toolbar button + panel** — a draggable panel that remembers its position: counters, the selected prop's name, a per-prop list for small selections (hover highlights the prop in the world, click isolates it), align controls, blueprints — every action clickable, with tooltips - All hotkeys rebindable, English and Serbian localization
## Usage Activate with **Ctrl+Shift+C** or the toolbar button. Click or drag-select props, **Ctrl+C** to copy, **Ctrl+V** to paste, click to place. Quick right-click steps back.
## Transparency AI-assisted development: the code was written with heavy use of AI tools (Claude Fable), directed, reviewed and hand-tested in-game by the author through many iterations. Full source code is public on GitHub (link below) — judge it freely. Bug reports are read and fixed by a human.
## Credits & thanks Copaste started as a personal tool and grew into this release. It stands on the shoulders of the CS2 modding community — written from scratch, with patterns and APIs learned from open-source mods whose MIT and Apache-2.0 licenses explicitly welcome that. Sincere thanks to:
- **yenyang** — the selection, highlighting and raycasting patterns were learned from the sources of *Better Bulldozer*, *Anarchy*, *Tree Controller* and *Move It*; Anarchy's PreventOverride is integrated at runtime when present - **algernon** — the object placement approach (the game's definition pipeline) was learned from the sources of *Line Tool* - **Bruceyboy24804** — *Node Controller* served as the reference for how mod UI integrates with the game's interface - **Colossal Order & Paradox** — for Cities: Skylines II and the official modding documentation - The **CS2 modding community** for keeping their mods open source — none of this would exist otherwise
### Special thanks A very special thank-you to **Biffa** (Biffa Plays Indie Games) and **ConflictNerd** — simply for being the author's favorite Cities: Skylines YouTubers and the reason this game never gets boring. Keep the traffic flowing!
Source code (MIT): https://github.com/viktorsx/Copaste
Publish.ChangeLog:
Panel redesign and quality-of-life update. Hand tested in game before publishing - that's the routine for every Copaste release.
Panel - Complete visual redesign: grouped cards, icons on every button, clear button states, readable counters - The panel can now be dragged by its header and remembers its position between sessions - Single click-selected props show their name in the panel (marquee selections don't) - Small selections (up to 15 props) get a Selected props list in the panel: hovering an entry rings that prop in the world, clicking it keeps only that prop selected - handy when a prop is hard to click directly - Blueprint and selected props lists are paged: 5 per page with arrows in the section header
Editing - Pasted props now keep the original's look by default - both the game's color variation and any custom color picked in the Customization tab. The Original/Random toggle in the panel restores the old random behavior - The paste preview shows the real colors too, instead of shuffling them while you move - Undo of a delete also restores the original colors now - New Align tools: Line makes a tidy row - straight line, equal gaps and all props rotated the same way; To prop does the same anchored to a reference prop you click (its position, facing and rotation); Circle arranges the selection evenly on a circle. The gap stepper sets exact meters; while an align button is lit, [ and ] keys (rebindable) or the stepper resize the layout live - Alt+drag moves a single prop out of the selection; Alt+mouse wheel spins every selected prop around its own axis (15 degree steps) - Ctrl+click cycles through props around the click point - picks up props partially buried in other objects or buildings that a normal click can never reach; click the same spot again to go to the next one - Move drag no longer jerks at the start - the selection follows the cursor smoothly from the first frame - Nudge (Ctrl+arrows) step halved for finer control
Blueprints - Blueprints now store color variations and custom colors too; older blueprint files still load fine
Options - Mod settings are now split into General and Key bindings tabs, with key bindings grouped by what they do
